newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto film festival adds "In & Out", "Fairytale".
newsitem.headline: Toronto film festival adds "In & Out", "Fairytale".

text.p: Frank Oz's "In and Out" and "Fairytale - A True Story" will have their world premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival, organizers said on Friday.
The films will be among the handful of gala presentations at the festival, which runs from September 4 to 13.
"In & Out" stars Kevin Kline as a smalltown high school teacher whose sexuality is called into question when a former student tells an Oscar telecast that Kline's character is gay.
The Frank Oz-directed film also stars Tom Selleck as a ruthless television reporter, Matt Dillon, Joan Cusack, and Debbie Reynolds.
"Fairytale", which is set during the First World War, stars Harvey Keitel as Harry Houdini and Peter O'Toole as Sherlock Holmes creator Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.
In the film the pair set out to investigate the story of two girls believed to have captured photographic evidence of fairies.
The movie is directed by Charles Sturridge, who debuted with his feature "Where Angels Fear to Tread" at a previous Toronto festival.

Films already confirmed as gala presentations include the North American premiere of director Curtis Hanson's "L.A. Confidential" and the world premiere of "Mrs Dalloway" by Dutch filmmaker Marleen Gorris. Gorris' last movie, "Antonia's Line", won an Academy Award for best foreign film.
